identity.real_world_identity_notes: One-make Supercup specification of the G55, classed separately by AMS2 as G55Supercup rather than GT4. It shares the platform and the six-speed Hewland gearbox and likewise requires the clutch to pull away, but it is recorded independently of the GT4 car rather than inherited from it.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
Unlike the dual-clutch cars in this batch the clutch is required to move off, which is consistent with a conventional racing gearbox rather than a PDK or DCT.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.ginetta-g55-gt4-supercup.20260813t170235026z-27deda7a by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is established by a registered manufacturer source.

claims.basis: The registered manufacturer source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The registered source establishes the G55 platform and its Hewland six-speed; the live drive confirmed six paddle-selected gears and that the clutch is required to move off. The source does not differentiate this variant's gearbox internals, so the construction is recorded conservatively as sequential.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

driver_summary: One-make Supercup G55, sharing the platform and the six-speed Hewland with the GT4 car and asking the same of the driver: it cuts and blips for itself, and the clutch is yours only to pull away.
